clue.text: Trade's so bad, even though diversified

indicators.note: trade being bad suggests these letters have gone wrong and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A merchant laments poor business despite having branched out into many lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' tells you to rearrange TRADESSO; 'even though' only links the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something diversified is varied or mixed, like an assorted box of chocolates.

clue.text: Pop back and call up the beastly fellow

indicators.note: pop back means the word for father is read backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, as is pop

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to name is to call

explanation.surface: A father returns and rings the brutish man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PA into AP; 'up' turns NAME into EMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An ape-man is a primitive, half-animal human, so a brutish creature of a man.

clue.text: From the outset terriers were the favoured breed of dog

indicators.note: from these words means the letters are taken out of a run spanning them

explanation.surface: From the beginning, terriers were the most popular dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' points to the run inside outSET TERriers.
explanation.definitionFit: The English, Irish and Gordon setters are gundog breeds.

clue.text: Stay behind with airmen in a mess

indicators.note: airmen in a mess are jumbled up, though a mess is also where servicemen eat

explanation.surface: An officer stays on with the aircrew in their dining hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a mess' rearranges AIRMEN; 'with' is a link. The surface uses mess as the forces' dining room.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain is to be left behind or to stay put.

clue.text: The origin of certain dental treatment

definitions.meaning: one's ancestry or descent, as in 'of Irish birth'

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both descent or lineage and the pulling of a tooth by a dentist.

clue.text: Writer accommodating English guide

indicators.note: a writer accommodating something holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Francis Bacon, the Elizabethan essayist and philosopher

explanation.surface: An author puts up an English tour guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodating' puts E inside BACON.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a signal light that directs ships or travellers, so it serves as a guide.

clue.text: Sense people rowing will encompass agreement

indicators.note: people who encompass something surround it, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen
yes is a word of agreement

explanation.surface: A rowing crew will reach consensus with common sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'people rowing' is a crew, not a verb phrase; 'will encompass' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is one of the five senses.

clue.text: Muse about everything-and that's including work

parts.note: c is circa, meaning about
all means everything

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is including the work means the work goes inside it

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is
op, opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone ponders the whole picture, work included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muse' looks like a verb meaning ponder but is one of the nine Muses; 'including' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Calliope is the Greek Muse of epic poetry, one of the nine goddesses of the arts.

clue.text: No mention's made about, for example, flower arrangements

indicators.note: the word is made about another means it is built round it

parts.note: says, as in 'he says', is a mention made

explanation.surface: Nobody comments on the floral displays.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'No mention's made' as nobody commenting; 'made about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small posy of flowers.

clue.text: Judge-one married in Oriental country

parts.note: E stands for East, so for Oriental

indicators.note: one married placed in the country means those letters go inside its word

parts.note: a state is a nation or country
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A judge, newly wed, settles in an Eastern land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts IM inside STATE, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a size or value roughly is to make a reckoning of it, which is to guess it closely.

clue.text: Workers around the fifties can be most attractive women

indicators.note: the workers placed around the fifties wrap their word round those letters

parts.note: worker bees, so bees stand for workers
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two of them make the fifties

explanation.surface: Women employed in their fifties can still be the most glamorous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the fifties' suggests age, but it is two Roman fifties; 'around' signals the container and 'can be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A belle is the outstanding beauty at a gathering, as in the belle of the ball.

clue.text: Statesmanlike?

parts.note: read not as dignified and political but as typical of a man from the States, the USA

explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the United States, often just called the States, is a citizen of that country.

clue.text: There's nothing to be said for acting in this way

definitions.text: There's nothing to be said for acting in this way

parts.words: There's nothing to be said for acting in this way
parts.note: not a dismissal of an acting style but a description of performing without speaking any words

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a particular style of acting as worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with gestures alone, saying nothing, is the art of the mime.

clue.text: Fighting heavyweight from a Northern town

parts.note: warring means fighting
a ton is a very heavy weight

explanation.surface: A boxing heavyweight hails from the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Warrington is a town in Cheshire, in the north-west of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Warrington is a large town between Liverpool and Manchester in north-west England.

clue.text: The pastry's made differently in the Scottish Highlands

indicators.note: the pastry made differently means its letters are formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A baker in the north of Scotland prepares pastry their own way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made differently' rearranges THEPASTRYS. Strathspey is the valley of the River Spey, an area of the Scottish Highlands; it also names a Scottish dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Strathspey is a district of the Highlands of Scotland, the broad valley of the River Spey.

clue.text: A summary of Jack's homily

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, as is an AB, so the sailor's gives a piece; read with A it forms AB's
a tract is a short moral essay, like a homily

explanation.surface: A précis of a sailor's sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstract is a short digest of a longer document.

clue.text: A number in quiet surroundings provide music

definitions.meaning: a song sung softly, as to a lover beneath her window at night
the verb, to sing or play to someone

explanation.surface: A piece played in peaceful surroundings gives music.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is an evening love song, and to sing one to someone is to woo with music.

clue.text: He daren't upset the one who follows

indicators.note: he being upset implies these letters are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A man too scared to offend his leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges HEDARENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter or follower of a cause or leader.

clue.text: Basis for cutting staple food

parts.note: bread is a staple food
board means meals provided, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Bread is the foundation for slicing a staple food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staple' looks like it goes with 'food', but each gives its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden slab on which loaves are sliced is the base for cutting them.

clue.text: Innate ability to make money

definitions.meaning: a weight of silver or gold used as currency in the ancient world

explanation.surface: Being born gifted is the way to get rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' is a link. The money sense is the ancient unit of currency in the Bible's parable of the talents.
explanation.definitionFit: It means both a natural gift and an ancient unit of coinage.

clue.text: Diana might appear about right for this guy

indicators.note: the reshuffled name goes about the right letter, holding it inside
Diana might appear in other forms, so her letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Diana might turn up and be right for this man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might appear' rearranges DIANA to ADIAN; 'about' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrian is a man's first name, so a fellow.

clue.text: An association that gives the French the shivers

parts.note: le is the French masculine form of the
ague is a feverish fit of shivering

explanation.surface: A society makes French people tremble.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is an alliance or union of members, like a sports league.

clue.text: A fine city-almost the finest of all

indicators.note: almost means the phrase is not quite complete, with its final letter left off

parts.note: the best is the finest of all

explanation.surface: A splendid city is nearly the greatest of them all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last T of THE BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a great city of ancient Egypt and also of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Remove the back seat

parts.note: not taking out a car's rear bench but taking off the seat that sits on a horse's back

explanation.surface: Someone takes out the rear seat of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking the saddle, the seat on a horse's back, off the animal.

clue.text: Brought down when installed in a place for the retired

indicators.note: one word installed in another is set inside it

parts.note: a bed is where those who have retired for the night lie
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone humbled on being placed in an old people's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'installed in' puts AS inside A BED; 'the retired' means those gone to bed, not pensioners.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abased is to be humbled or lowered in dignity.

clue.text: Being a director, always in smart environs

indicators.note: always in smart means the first word goes inside the second

parts.note: to smart is to sting
eer is a poetic shortening of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A company director is always well dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' looks like an adjective for clothes but is the verb meaning to hurt; 'in' signals the container, 'environs' merely reinforcing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Steering a vehicle or venture means guiding it, which is what one who directs does.

clue.text: The score is two-nil

parts.note: not a football result but the figures 2 and 0 written side by side, giving the number a score stands for

explanation.surface: A football reporter gives the match result.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is a set of twenty, and the digits two and nought written together make 20.

clue.text: Woven cane isn't used in this case

indicators.note: cane that is woven is twisted together, so these letters are interlaced into a new order

explanation.surface: In this basket, woven cane is not the material used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woven' rearranges CANEISNT; 'used in this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is an example or occurrence, as in 'in this case' or 'for instance'.
